channel.title: Newspin: latest timeline updates
channel.description: Newspin turns the biggest ongoing news stories in India, the US and around the world into clear, sourced timelines: what happened, when, and what comes next.

item.title: Ukraine talks: Kushner says Russia accepts Europe at the table; Moscow rejects any NATO-style role for Kyiv
item.description: 19–20 Nov 2026 · After the Berlin meeting of Ukraine's allies, US envoy Jared Kushner said: 'I think we've gotten the Russians comfortable with that concept where any security guarantee for Ukraine would be based on Article 5.' Article 5 is NATO's rule that an attack on one member is an attack on all. He also said Russia had agreed to talks that include Europe. Moscow has not confirmed this. Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Sergei Ryabkov said any 'quasi membership' of NATO for Kyiv was 'totally unacceptable', and that a visit by European representatives was 'under consideration'. Zelenskyy said the next meeting would be four-way: Ukraine, the US, Russia and Europe. No date has been set.

item.title: Ukraine talks: Russia strikes three Kyiv bridges after Putin promises a response
item.description: 20 Nov 2026 · Overnight Russian ballistic missiles damaged the Podilskyi, Darnytskyi and Southern bridges over the Dnipro in Kyiv, Mayor Vitali Klitschko said. Traffic was restricted and people crossed the river on foot. Prime Minister Koretskyi said eight people were killed, six of them in Kyiv, and 28 wounded. Russia's Defence Ministry said it targeted bridges used to move weapons, plus defence, energy and transport sites. Power was cut across Kyiv and in 10 regions after nuclear plants reduced output, Ukraine's energy ministry said. Putin had said in China: 'We will respond to these attacks.'

item.title: Nvidia & Huang: Reuters: SEC staff examining possible accounting issues at Nvidia; shares fall 14%
item.description: 20 Nov 2026 (US time) · Two people briefed on the matter told Reuters that enforcement staff at the SEC, the US markets regulator, are examining "potential accounting issues" at Nvidia. Reuters could not find out when the inquiry began or which issues it covers. The Wall Street Journal had reported an SEC probe on 17 November without saying what it focused on. The SEC declined to comment and Nvidia did not immediately respond, per Reuters. An inquiry is not a finding of wrongdoing, and many end without action. Nvidia shares closed down 14.01% at $125.53, per Yahoo Finance and CappNotes, the worst day since January 2025, per CappNotes. Reuters, citing LSEG data, says shares were already down more than 6% before its report.

item.title: AI this week: AI shares slide as Reuters reports SEC probe of Nvidia's accounting
item.description: 20 Nov 2026 (US time) · Reuters reported, citing two people briefed on the matter, that staff at the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) are examining possible accounting issues at Nvidia. Reuters could not say when the inquiry began or which practices are being reviewed. The SEC declined to comment. An investigation is not proof of wrongdoing. Nvidia's shares fell sharply, and the Motley Fool estimated about $491 billion of its market value was wiped out in a day. Anthropic's shares fell to within five cents of their $83 IPO price before closing at about $88 to $89 ($88.91 per Yahoo Finance and CappNotes, $88.30 per 24/7 Wall St).

item.title: Anthropic: Shares fall back towards the IPO price on day two
item.description: 20 Nov 2026 (US time) · On its second day of trading, Anthropic's share price fell as low as $83.05, five cents above the $83 IPO price, per 24/7 Wall St and Startup Fortune. It then recovered to close at about $88 to $89: $88.91 (−8.50%) per Yahoo Finance and CappNotes, $88.30 per 24/7 Wall St. That is roughly 9% below Thursday's close of $97.17 but still about 6% to 7% above the IPO price. The fall came as AI and chip stocks sold off for a second day: Nvidia's shares fell sharply after Reuters reported that the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) is looking into its accounting. Startup Fortune also pointed to worries that AI companies' valuations have run ahead of their profits.

item.title: West Asia & oil: Oil heads for a third weekly fall as Gulf exports recover
item.description: 20 Nov 2026 · Oil prices were on course for a third weekly fall in a row on Friday, Reuters reported via RTÉ, as crude shipments through the Strait of Hormuz have returned to roughly pre-war levels, raising expectations of a supply surplus. Brent fell below $91 a barrel by 11 am New York time, per Al-Monitor, and PTI reported it 1.82% lower at $90.31 during Indian trading hours. Earlier in the day, Brent had risen to $92.57 after a Houthi missile attack on Riyadh and an Iranian Revolutionary Guards claim that two tankers hit mines in Hormuz and were burning; that claim has not been independently confirmed. Saxo analysts also pointed to a sell-off in AI-linked shares weighing on demand expectations. UOB analysts say Iranian attacks on tankers are running at about one a day in November. OPEC+ meets on 29 November.

item.title: US markets: S&P 500 falls 3.7% for a seventh straight loss and enters a correction; Nasdaq turns negative for 2026
item.description: 20 Nov 2026 · The S&P 500 fell 3.70% to 6,910.39, its seventh loss in a row, per Yahoo Finance and CappNotes. It closed about 10.7% below its record close of 7,818.93 on 6 October, which counts as a correction (a fall of 10% or more from a peak). The Dow fell 1.93% and also closed in a correction. The Nasdaq fell 5.28% and is now down for 2026. CappNotes puts the S&P 500's fall for the week at 8.6%, its worst week since April 2025. Reporters linked the fall to a sell-off in AI and chip shares and to expectations that the Fed will raise rates in December. Nvidia fell 14.01%; CappNotes cites a Reuters report that SEC enforcement staff are examining possible accounting issues at the company. AMD fell 13.25%. Anthropic fell 8.50% to $88.91 on its second day of trading, still above its $83 IPO price. Consumer staples was the only sector to rise, per CappNotes. Opening levels were not given, so this day has no gap figure; Yahoo Finance reports the S&P 500 was down about 0.5% soon after the open.

item.title: Starship: Debris on a Mexican beach; SpaceX says it found very little
item.description: 17–19 Nov 2026 · Mexico's federal environment agency, Profepa, said debris began washing up on Playa Bagdad in Tamaulipas, just across the border from Starbase, on the morning of 17 November, after the Flight 15 booster came down in the Gulf of Mexico. Profepa said it would take custody of the material and ask SpaceX to take responsibility for anything traced to its launches. The conservation group Conibio reported plastic, tape and adhesive fragments offshore. On 19 November SpaceX said its teams found very few fragments, that their origin was not confirmed, and that social media claims of widespread damage were false or misleading. It cited independent tests finding no chemical, biological or toxicological risk in Starship's materials and offered to help if Mexican authorities ask. Investigators have not yet said which pieces came from Flight 15.

item.title: Online gaming: Supreme Court to hear the challenge to the ban on 2 December
item.description: 19 Nov 2026 · The company behind the A23 Rummy app, the lead petitioner challenging the 2025 gaming law, asked the Supreme Court for an earlier hearing, and a bench led by Chief Justice Surya Kant listed the case for 2 December, gaming trade outlets report. The petitioners argue the law wrongly treats games of skill like games of chance, breaks the right to do business, and covers betting, which the Constitution leaves to states. The case was moved to the Supreme Court from three High Courts in September 2025 and has been deferred before. A hearing date is not a stay: the ban stays in force unless the court rules otherwise.

item.title: Google Gemini: Genie 4 world model opens to Ultra subscribers
item.description: 18 Nov 2026 (US time) · Google DeepMind made Genie 4, its newest 'world model', available in Project Genie, a browser-based experiment. Instead of playing back a finished video, it builds a scene as the user moves through it. Users can type prompts to change the weather, add characters or steer events, and for the first time it generates sound. It is open to eligible Google AI Ultra subscribers, a plan that costs $199.99 a month in the US, per Decrypt; AI Pro subscribers can join a waitlist. The Next Web notes that details can drift in long sessions.

item.title: US trade deal: Commerce Secretary: deal 'more or less finalised' but can't be signed until new US tariff rules are in place
item.description: 18 Nov 2026 · Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal said "every aspect of the deal has been more or less finalised" and negotiations will conclude soon. But he said the two countries cannot sign it until Washington puts its new tariff structure in place: "Till that tariff architecture is in place, the countries won't be able to sign the deal." The US is rebuilding its tariffs after its Supreme Court ruled in February that the emergency law used for the earlier tariffs did not allow them. Agrawal also pointed to pending US Section 301 investigations, saying countries will want to know their outcome before signing. He spoke at a FICCI event in New Delhi, per ANI.

item.title: Founder comebacks: Huang says he would be 'honored' to return; the board chair says no
item.description: 17 Nov 2026 (US time) · In his first public statement since resigning, Huang said he had "made serious mistakes" in his personal life and would be "honored" to return as CEO if the board decides that is in the best interest of shareholders, employees, the company and America. On Nvidia's earnings call the same day, board chair Harvey Jones said "the Nvidia board does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO", per Constellation Research. CBS News, citing a person familiar with the board's thinking, also reports the board is against his return.

item.title: China's AI labs: Nvidia stops shipping US-approved H200 chips to China
item.description: 17 Nov 2026 (US time) · Nvidia's interim CEO Colette Kress said on the company's earnings call that it is "no longer shipping licensed Hopper data centre products to China", which include the H200 chips Washington had approved for some Chinese buyers, Reuters reported. Nvidia sold $2.4 billion of these chips to China in the quarter to 25 October, and its forecast includes none. She did not say why or whether the halt is permanent. Beijing has also limited imports of the H200 to cut reliance on US technology. For Chinese AI labs, it means less new supply of the US chips used to train and run large models.

item.title: US midterms: AP calls Alaska's Senate race for Peltola, the last Senate race to be decided
item.description: 17 Nov 2026 · The Associated Press called Alaska's US Senate race for Democrat Mary Peltola over Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan on the evening of 17 November, Alaska time. In the latest count Peltola had 144,302 votes (50.12%) to Sullivan's 131,844, Alaska's News Source reports. Because she passed 50%, Alaska's ranked-choice second round was not needed. AP says it was the last Senate race of the midterms to be decided. Sullivan's campaign said it would not comment until all ballots were counted. The result has not yet been certified.

item.title: Founder comebacks: Reports say Huang is discussing a comeback
item.description: 15 Nov 2026 · The Financial Times reported, citing people familiar with the matter, that Huang has discussed returning as Nvidia's chief executive with confidants, according to Reuters and The Next Web. Two Nvidia investors posted a letter to the board urging a search that includes "the potential return of Jensen Huang", The Next Web reports. The same day, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Nvidia should look outside the company for a new CEO, per Fortune.

item.title: xAI & Grok: About 60 jobs reportedly cut from the Grok Imagine video team
item.description: 13 Nov 2026 · SpaceX's AI group cut about 60 roles from the team behind Grok Imagine, its image and video generator, leaving only a handful of staff, The Information reported, citing people familiar with the matter. Summaries of the report say the group is putting more effort into coding tools and its Grok Bot agent. Grok Imagine is still available to users. SpaceX has not commented publicly.

item.title: Founder comebacks: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO
item.description: 12 Nov 2026 · Nvidia says its co-founder Jensen Huang has stepped down as chief executive after a board meeting, amid reports linking him to Chinese intelligence and a board investigation. Chief financial officer Colette Kress becomes interim CEO. The board is reported to be looking at outside candidates for the permanent job. The full story is in Newspin's Nvidia timeline.

item.title: Electricity policy: Draft sent to the Cabinet for inter-ministry review
item.description: 24 Sep 2026 · Power Secretary Pankaj Agarwal said the ministry had moved a Cabinet note so other ministries can review the draft policy, after stakeholder comments were compiled. "I think it won't be taking very long," he said at a FICCI power conference. After this review, the government will issue the final policy. The policy it replaces dates from 2005.

item.title: Founder comebacks: Altman rejoins OpenAI's board after review
item.description: 8 Mar 2024 · OpenAI said a review by law firm WilmerHale was complete and that Altman would rejoin the board. According to OpenAI's summary, the review found "a breakdown in trust" between the old board and Altman. It said the old board acted within its discretion but his conduct did not require removal. OpenAI also added three new board members.

item.title: Founder comebacks: OpenAI agrees to bring Altman back as CEO
item.description: 21 Nov 2023 · Late on 21 November (US time), OpenAI said it had "reached an agreement in principle" for Altman to return as chief executive with a new initial board. Bret Taylor would chair it, with Larry Summers and Adam D'Angelo. Days earlier, Microsoft had said Altman would join it, and most OpenAI staff had signed a letter calling for the board to resign. OpenAI confirmed Altman's return as CEO on 29 November and gave Microsoft a non-voting seat on the board.

item.title: Founder comebacks: OpenAI board removes Sam Altman as CEO
item.description: 17 Nov 2023 · OpenAI's board removed co-founder Sam Altman as chief executive. The board said he "was not consistently candid in his communications with the board" and that it no longer had confidence in his ability to lead OpenAI. Chief technology officer Mira Murati became interim CEO. Greg Brockman stepped down as board chair and later said he had quit.

item.title: Founder comebacks: Schultz hands over to Laxman Narasimhan
item.description: 20 Mar 2023 · Laxman Narasimhan became Starbucks CEO on 20 March 2023, nearly two weeks earlier than the planned 1 April start, CNBC reported. This ended Schultz's third spell as chief executive. CNBC reported that in September 2022 Schultz said he would never return as CEO again.

item.title: Founder comebacks: Schultz returns again, as interim CEO
item.description: 4 Apr 2022 · Starbucks said on 16 March 2022 that CEO Kevin Johnson would retire and Schultz would return as interim chief executive. Schultz took over on 4 April. He was paid $1 for the role, according to CNBC and NPR. It was his third spell as CEO.

item.title: Founder comebacks: Dorsey steps down as Twitter CEO for good
item.description: 29 Nov 2021 · Dorsey stepped down as chief executive. Chief technology officer Parag Agrawal took over, effective immediately, according to Axios. Dorsey said: "I've decided to leave Twitter because I believe the company is ready to move on from its founders." He said he would stay on the board until his term ended in 2022.

item.title: Founder comebacks: Page steps down as Alphabet CEO
item.description: 3 Dec 2019 · Page steps down as Alphabet's chief executive and Brin as its president, effective immediately. Both stay on the board and remain shareholders. Sundar Pichai becomes CEO of both Google and Alphabet. "We've never been ones to hold on to management roles when we think there's a better way to run the company," the founders wrote.

item.title: Founder comebacks: Schultz hands CEO role to Kevin Johnson
item.description: 3 Apr 2017 · Starbucks announced on 1 December 2016 that Schultz would step down as CEO. President and chief operating officer Kevin Johnson took over on 3 April 2017. Schultz became executive chairman, working on the company's Reserve Roasteries. 'Kevin and the team are in charge,' Schultz said, according to NPR.

item.title: Founder comebacks: Twitter makes Dorsey its permanent CEO
item.description: 5 Oct 2015 · Twitter named Dorsey permanent chief executive. He kept running Square at the same time. Board member Peter Currie said: "We didn't get to a different answer until we saw Jack at work for three months." Twitter said in a filing there were no plans to pay Dorsey directly for the CEO role.

item.title: Founder comebacks: Page becomes CEO of the new Alphabet
item.description: 10 Aug 2015 · Page announces Alphabet, a new parent company with Google as its largest part. Page becomes Alphabet's chief executive and Brin its president. Sundar Pichai becomes CEO of Google.

item.title: Founder comebacks: Dorsey returns as Twitter's interim CEO
item.description: 1 Jul 2015 · Dorsey took over as interim chief executive of Twitter after Dick Costolo stepped down. Twitter had announced the change on 11 June 2015 and said the board would look for a new chief executive. Dorsey stayed on as CEO of Square, the payments company he co-founded in 2009.

item.title: Founder comebacks: Yang leaves Yahoo altogether
item.description: 17 Jan 2012 · Yang resigned from Yahoo's board and all other positions at the company, effective 17 January 2012, according to Yahoo's filing. CNN reported he also left the boards of Yahoo Japan and Alibaba.

item.title: Founder comebacks: Jobs resigns as CEO; Tim Cook takes over
item.description: 24 Aug 2011 · Jobs resigns as Apple's chief executive and recommends chief operating officer Tim Cook to succeed him. The board names Cook CEO and elects Jobs chairman. Jobs died on 5 October 2011.

item.title: Founder comebacks: Page returns as Google's CEO
item.description: 4 Apr 2011 · Google announced on 20 January 2011 that Page would replace Schmidt. The change took effect on 4 April. Schmidt became executive chairman, working on outside partners and government relations. Schmidt wrote on Twitter that "day to day adult supervision is no longer needed", NPR reported.

item.title: Founder comebacks: Carol Bartz replaces Yang as Yahoo CEO
item.description: 13 Jan 2009 · Yahoo named former Autodesk chief Carol Bartz as CEO, effective immediately. Yang went back to his 'Chief Yahoo' role. In 2008 Yang had rejected a Microsoft takeover bid, and Yahoo's profit fell 64% in the third quarter of that year, The Register reported.

item.title: Founder comebacks: Yang says he will step down as CEO
item.description: 17 Nov 2008 · Yahoo said Yang had decided to step down as CEO once the board found a successor. He would go back to being 'Chief Yahoo' and stay on the board. Yahoo said Yang and the board agreed the timing. Al Jazeera reported that Yang was blamed for the collapse of a deal with Microsoft.

item.title: Founder comebacks: Jack Dorsey replaced as Twitter CEO
item.description: 16 Oct 2008 · Twitter co-founder Jack Dorsey left the chief executive job. Co-founder Evan Williams took over. At the time Williams said "Jack remains Chairman" and that Twitter needed "a focused approach from a single leader". Later accounts, based on Nick Bilton's book "Hatching Twitter", say the board fired Dorsey over concerns about his management.

item.title: Founder comebacks: Schwab hands CEO role to Walt Bettinger
item.description: 1 Oct 2008 · The board named president and chief operating officer Walt Bettinger as CEO from 1 October 2008. The decision was announced in July 2008. Schwab, then 70, stayed on as chairman, Reuters reported.

item.title: Founder comebacks: Schultz returns as Starbucks CEO
item.description: 7 Jan 2008 · Starbucks' board made chairman Howard Schultz chief executive again, effective immediately. He replaced Jim Donald, who had been CEO since 2005. Starbucks' shares had fallen about 50% over the previous year and US store traffic was declining, the Associated Press reported. Schultz said he was returning 'for the long term'.

item.title: Founder comebacks: Co-founder Jerry Yang takes over as Yahoo CEO
item.description: 18 Jun 2007 · Jerry Yang co-founded Yahoo with David Filo in 1994 but had never been its chief executive. His title was 'Chief Yahoo'. On 18 June 2007 Terry Semel resigned as CEO and the board named Yang in his place, effective that day, according to Yahoo's filing. Shareholders were unhappy about a nearly 30% fall in Yahoo's share price over 18 months, Al Jazeera reported.

item.title: Founder comebacks: Michael Dell returns as CEO after Rollins resigns
item.description: 31 Jan 2007 · Kevin Rollins resigns as chief executive and leaves the board, effective immediately. Michael Dell takes over as CEO and stays chairman. The return came after HP overtook Dell as the world's biggest PC seller, according to Computerworld, citing Gartner, and while the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) was investigating Dell's accounting. The board said there was "no better person in the world to run Dell at this time".

item.title: Founder comebacks: Schwab returns as CEO as Pottruck leaves
item.description: 20 Jul 2004 · The board removed Pottruck as CEO and reappointed Charles Schwab, effective immediately. Pottruck said: 'I accept the Board's decision that it's time for me to step aside.' The news came with second-quarter results showing profit down 10%, the Las Vegas Sun reported.
